prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web application concept for Wicker Study Tutor, 1440 × 900 landscape
Primary request: Design the "Situation Desk" Tutor page as a credible production UI, not a poster. The student asked: "I plan to miss Tuesday because of work. What do I need to take care of?" The assistant has checked timetable, syllabi, Canvas assignments, announcements, academic calendar, and progress, then produced a concise actionable academic brief. Nothing executes without consent.
Input image: existing Wicker Study Practice page; carry over its exact app shell, warm off-white canvas, left sidebar, Archivo/Archivo Narrow feeling, navy ink, indigo action color, thin full-span rules, corner language and density. Do not copy the Practice content or question card.
Composition: persistent existing Wicker left navigation sidebar. Main Tutor workspace uses a broad 2-column split: approximately 72% conversation/briefing sheet and 28% action docket. At top of main area: page title "Tutor", a small workspace scope control "All courses", and a conversation history button. Main answer area starts with the user's short message, then a strong assistant response titled "Tuesday absence brief". Show four clear ruled findings: "Mandatory lab · BCS1540 · 10:45", "Group project check-in · BCS1520", "Quiz closes · 23:59", "Lecture recording available". Use restrained status labels such as "Action needed" and "Covered". At the bottom of the answer place one collapsed, full-width disclosure row "Evidence · 8 sources" with a chevron; citations are visible only when expanded.
Right action docket: header "Proposed actions", then 3 serious flat rows with checkboxes or status markers: "Message project group", "Move Statistics practice", "Remember I am unavailable Tuesday". Each row states what will happen. Footer has secondary "Dismiss" and primary indigo "Review 3 actions". Show a small notice: "Nothing changes until you approve."
Bottom: wide fixed message composer with context line "Workspace-wide · currently checking all courses", attachment button, and primary send arrow.
Visual hierarchy: the response itself is primary; the action docket is quieter. Use full-span internal borders that reach panel edges. Avoid borders ending within padded content. Avoid nested card stacks. No gradients, glass, excessive shadows, bubbles for assistant content, oversized empty regions, or decorative illustration. Keep all UI text legible and spell the supplied text exactly. The result must visibly read as an academic tutor workspace for evidence-backed explanations and consented actions.
